sections.markdown:
## C2 — Arrow and lane-use signals, roundabouts and confusables

FACT_ID: sec09-F29 | anchor: A57
Arrows control specific turning movements, and yellow and green arrows give left turns the same control that the standard light gives through traffic. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec09-F30 | anchor: A57
A green arrow lets you go in the arrow's direction while opposing traffic has to stop. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec09-F31 | anchor: A57
A steady green arrow, alone or with other lights, lets you enter for the arrow's movement or any other movement the other lights allow, still yielding to pedestrians and vehicles lawfully in the intersection. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec09-F32 | anchor: A57
Yellow arrows follow green arrows to show the protected movement is ending, and a steady yellow arrow shown with a circular green means that protected turn is ending. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec09-F33 | anchor: A58
A steady yellow arrow shown alone or with a steady circular red clears the protected turn, and you may not enter the intersection after it goes out. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec09-F34 | anchor: A58
Lane use control signals hang over individual lanes of a street, highway or freeway to show which lanes you may or may not use. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec09-F35 | anchor: A58
A steady red X over a lane means you may not drive in that lane, and it overrides the other traffic controls there accordingly. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec09-F36 | anchor: A58
A steady green arrow over a lane means you may drive in that lane while obeying all other controls and normal safe practice. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec09-F37 | anchor: A58
The manual says a steady yellow X lets you drive in that lane only with caution, because it signals potentially hazardous conditions. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec09-F38 | anchor: A59
Roundabouts are spreading in the U.S. because one-way counterclockwise flow creates fewer conflict points and moves traffic more safely and efficiently than standard intersections. [A59]
Source: [A59 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-F39 | anchor: A59
Compared with other intersection controls, roundabouts cut fatal crashes about 90%, injury crashes about 75% and all crashes about 35%, according to the crash statistics the manual cites. [A59]
Source: [A59 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-F40 | anchor: A59
To drive a roundabout, slow down, obey the signs, and yield to pedestrians and bicyclists before you enter. [A59]
Source: [A59 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-F41 | anchor: A59
Yield to traffic coming from your left that is already in the roundabout, and enter only when there is a safe gap. [A59]
Why it matters: the yield is owed to traffic on your left, already circling, not to traffic waiting to enter.
Source: [A59 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-F42 | anchor: A59
Keep your speed low inside the roundabout and turn off onto your road as you reach its exit. [A59]
Source: [A59 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-F43 | anchor: A59
At a roundabout, pedestrians at the curb look left for oncoming traffic, while those on the crosswalk island look right. [A59]
Source: [A59 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-F44 | anchor: A59
Bicyclists may ride through the roundabout or use the crosswalk instead. [A59]
Source: [A59 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-F45 | anchor: A60
Yield to pedestrians and bicycles as you leave the roundabout. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-F46 | anchor: A60
If you miss your exit, go around the roundabout again, and never back up inside it. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-F47 | anchor: A60
For an emergency vehicle, pull over before entering if you are not yet in the roundabout; if you are already in, continue to your exit and then pull over, avoiding any stop inside. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-F48 | anchor: A60
A truck apron is a paved area on the inside of a roundabout for the rear wheels of large trucks, and cars, pickups and SUVs are not meant to use it. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-F49 | anchor: A60
Vehicles already in a roundabout have the right-of-way. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-F50 | anchor: A60
Never turn left to enter a roundabout; wait for a safe gap and turn right into it. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-F51 | anchor: A60
Once inside a roundabout, do not stop unless stopping is the only way to avoid a crash or other danger. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-F52 | anchor: A60
In a two-lane roundabout, pick your lane and yield to traffic in both lanes before you enter. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-F53 | anchor: A60
In a two-lane roundabout, use the right lane for right turns and the left lane for left turns and U-turns, and to go straight follow the pavement markings, arrows or signs. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-R01 | anchor: A54
A solid yellow line on your side bans your passing, two solid yellow lines ban passing both ways, and a broken line alone allows passing when safe. [A54]
Why it matters: group_hint centerline-passing; prereq_hint sec09-F09; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec09-F10, sec09-F11, sec09-F12.
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-R02 | anchor: A58
Over a lane, a red X closes it, a green arrow opens it, and a yellow X allows it only with caution. [A58]
Why it matters: group_hint lane-use-signals; prereq_hint sec09-F34; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec09-F35, sec09-F36, sec09-F37.
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec09-R03 | anchor: A57
A green arrow is a protected turn with opposing traffic stopped, and a yellow arrow means that protection is ending. [A57]
Why it matters: group_hint turn-arrows; prereq_hint sec09-F29; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec09-F30, sec09-F32.
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec09-R04 | anchor: A60
An emergency vehicle means pull over if you have not entered the roundabout, but keep going to your exit first if you are already inside. [A60]
Why it matters: group_hint roundabout-emergency; prereq_hint sec09-F49; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec09-F47, sec09-F51.
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0060]
